name: SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct
creator: Hugging Face
blurb: A pocket-size assistant that fits almost any computer, even a very old one.
strengths: Runs on almost anything, including CPU-only laptops and mini PCs
Quick replies, low battery cost, tiny download
Fully open Apache 2.0 - no strings attached
weaknesses: Shallow answers on hard questions
Loses the thread in long conversations
Can be confidently wrong

verdict.text: If your machine struggled with the last decade, start here - proof that your laptop can still run AI.

name: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
creator: Meta
blurb: Meta's smallest Llama, built for phones and old laptops - handy for quick edits and summaries.
strengths: Tiny download that installs in minutes
Good at short rewrites, summaries, and quick drafts
Works on surprisingly little hardware
weaknesses: Makes things up more often than bigger models
Weak at math and coding

verdict.text: A zero-pressure starter: if this runs on your machine, everything bigger will too.

name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
creator: Meta
blurb: The 'just works everywhere' small Llama - a real assistant that still runs on modest laptops.
strengths: Noticeably smarter than the 1B model
Reliable for summaries, email drafts, and everyday questions
Huge ecosystem of community variants
weaknesses: Still limited on tricky reasoning and code
On 4 GB machines it may feel cramped

verdict.text: The best first real assistant if you'd rather not buy more RAM.

name: Phi-4-mini Instruct
creator: Microsoft
blurb: Microsoft's compact reasoner - small, quick, and unusually good at math for its size.
strengths: Strong math and logic for its size class
Comfortably fast on plain CPUs
Very open MIT license
weaknesses: Tuned for reasoning more than casual chat
Shorter default context than many peers

verdict.text: A sharp little brain for homework-style problems on modest hardware.

name: Gemma 3 4B
creator: Google
blurb: Google's small multimodal Gemma - it reads screenshots and photos, not just text.
license: Gemma Terms of Use (free with conditions)
strengths: Handles images plus text in one model
128K-token context window
Big-company polish in a small footprint
weaknesses: Outclassed on deep questions by its 12B and 27B siblings
Hugging Face requires accepting the license before download

verdict.text: The easiest way to try image understanding on modest hardware.

name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3
creator: Mistral AI
blurb: The classic that popularized small open models - still dependable, though newer rivals are sharper.
strengths: Proven and heavily supported by every local AI app
Fast for its size
Permissive Apache 2.0 license
weaknesses: Knowledge is dated (this version shipped in 2024)
Reasoning trails the newer 7-8B generation

verdict.text: A safe older workhorse - pick a newer 7-8B if you want maximum quality.

name: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
creator: Qwen (Alibaba)
blurb: An excellent all-rounder with unusually strong multilingual and structured-output skills.
strengths: Great at following exact instructions, lists, and JSON
Strong in many non-English languages
Mature ecosystem of fine-tunes and tools
weaknesses: Knowledge is older than it may feel
Occasionally over-refuses innocent requests

verdict.text: The dependable hatchback of local AI - not flashy, rarely lets you down.

name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
creator: Meta
blurb: The model that made local AI mainstream - balanced, friendly, backed by the biggest ecosystem.
strengths: All-purpose: chat, writing, light coding
128K-token context window
Supported by virtually every local AI tool
weaknesses: Knowledge stops around 2023
Sometimes stiff or wordy in tone

verdict.text: If you install one model ever, make it this - the local-AI default.

name: Qwen3 8B
creator: Qwen (Alibaba)
blurb: Qwen's newer all-rounder with a built-in 'think step by step' mode you can switch on or off.
strengths: Reasoning toggle: deep-think mode or fast chat mode
Improved multilingual understanding over Qwen2.5
Permissive Apache 2.0 license
weaknesses: Thinking mode can be slow and chatty on trivial prompts
Likes to over-explain unless redirected

verdict.text: A quality bump over the classic 8B crowd - an easy upgrade pick.

name: OLMo 2 7B Instruct
creator: Allen Institute for AI
blurb: The fully transparent option - open weights plus open training data, code, and recipes.
strengths: Most open lineage available: data, code, and weights are all public
No licensing puzzles, ever
Documentation that teaches how it was built
weaknesses: Raw quality trails Llama and Qwen at the same size
Smaller third-party ecosystem

verdict.text: For tinkerers and privacy purists who value openness as much as output.

name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill Qwen 7B
creator: DeepSeek
blurb: A compact reasoning model that shows its work - math and logic beyond its weight class.
strengths: Readable step-by-step chains of thought
Strong at math and logic puzzles
Open MIT-style license on the distill cards
weaknesses: Long 'thinking' delays before the answer
Meta-commentary is not ideal for quick chats

verdict.text: When you need a thinker, not a chatter.

name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct
creator: Qwen (Alibaba)
blurb: A specialist coding model that punches far above its size - the engine behind many AI code tools.
strengths: Excellent code generation and fix suggestions for its size
Works well inside editor plugins like Continue.dev
Permissive license for both personal and team use
weaknesses: Not a general chat companion
Narrow focus if you want variety

verdict.text: The default local coding co-pilot for 8 GB machines.

name: Phi-4 (14B)
creator: Microsoft
blurb: Microsoft's 14B reasoning gem - graduate-level math and careful logic on a single gaming GPU.
strengths: Top-tier math and logic per gigabyte in its class
Very open MIT license
Efficient - fast on one 8-12 GB VRAM GPU
weaknesses: Shorter context window than most peers
Stiffer persona - more precise than warm

verdict.text: When you want precise answers, not prose.

name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill Qwen 14B
creator: DeepSeek
blurb: The mid-size deep-thinker - sharper problem solving while still fitting a 16 GB machine.
strengths: High reasoning quality on consumer hardware
Readable line-by-line reasoning you can check
Strong at math, planning, and analysis
weaknesses: Slower replies because it thinks out loud
Long rambles can burn through context

verdict.text: A study buddy for algebra, proofs, and plan-making.

name: Llama 3.2 11B Vision
creator: Meta
blurb: Meta's photo-literate Llama - describe images and read charts and screenshots in plain text.
strengths: Decent image understanding plus strong text skills
Useful for describing photos and on-screen charts
Well supported in the Llama ecosystem
weaknesses: Vision skills trail newer dedicated image models
Image work increases RAM needs

verdict.text: Adds eyes to your setup without a huge download.

name: Gemma 3 12B
creator: Google
blurb: The Goldilocks Gemma - noticeably smarter than the small models, still laptop-sized.
license: Gemma Terms of Use (free with conditions)
strengths: Excellent chat and writing quality for its size
Image input included
Refined, polite tone out of the box
weaknesses: 12 GB machines will feel the strain
Not a reasoning specialist

verdict.text: The sweet spot once your machine has a little headroom.

name: Mistral Small 3.2 (24B)
creator: Mistral AI
blurb: Mistral's mid-size sweet spot - near-frontier feel with real multimodal eyes and Apache freedom.
strengths: Quality that feels close to much bigger rivals
Handles images as well as text
Permissive Apache 2.0 license
weaknesses: Wants 16 GB of RAM or a decent GPU
Overkill for light typing tasks

verdict.text: The upgrade that makes people ask 'wait, this runs at home?'

name: Gemma 3 27B
creator: Google
blurb: Google's big single-GPU flagship - the chat-quality ceiling for consumer rigs.
license: Gemma Terms of Use (free with conditions)
strengths: Best-in-class open chat quality in this size band
Image input included
Plenty of context headroom
weaknesses: Needs serious RAM or VRAM
Slow on CPU alone

verdict.text: Worth building a machine around - not your first week's model.

name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
creator: Meta
blurb: Meta's 70B flagship that trades punches with hosted frontier models - if your hardware is ready.
strengths: Near-frontier chat and coding, fully offline
Strong long-context behavior
Runs on a single high-end GPU with quantization
weaknesses: 40+ GB download and a long first run
Needs 32 GB of RAM minimum and is much happier with 64 or dual GPUs

verdict.text: The 'build the machine, then be amazed' pick - amazing once, not for your first week.
